scenes.tts: Without Notch, a fly embryo builds too much nervous system and too little skin. Notch is what lets a cell be told, not you. But the message never leaves the cell that makes it. The ligand is a protein fixed in that cell's membrane, and the receptor is fixed in its neighbour's. The two can meet only where cells touch.
scenes.visual: A row of cells without Notch, nearly all labelled nerve; two neighbours remain and a not-you message cannot cross between them; they become a sending and a receiving cell with a ligand and a receptor fixed in their membranes, which meet only when the cells touch.
scenes.narration: Without Notch, a fly embryo builds too much nervous system and too little skin. Notch is what lets a cell be told, not you. But the message never leaves the cell that makes it. The ligand is a protein fixed in that cell's membrane, and the receptor is fixed in its neighbour's. The two can meet only where cells touch.

scenes.tts: Binding is not enough. Just outside the membrane, Notch is folded into a lock that hides the spot where it can be cut. In the standard account, the receptor must be pulled. The sending cell draws its ligand back inside, and the tug passes to the receptor it holds. The pull peels the lock open.
scenes.visual: Zoom on the bound pair; the lock of small modules is marked over the hidden cut spot; the sending cell draws the ligand inward, the receptor is tugged, and the lock peels open to expose the spot.
scenes.narration: Binding is not enough. Just outside the membrane, Notch is folded into a lock that hides the spot where it can be cut. In the standard account, the receptor must be pulled. The sending cell draws its ligand back inside, and the tug passes to the receptor it holds. The pull peels the lock open.

scenes.tts: In mammalian cells, the first cut comes while the receptor is made, and it carries no signal. After the pull, an Adam protease makes the second cut, just outside the membrane. The outer part leaves with the ligand, and a stub stays in the membrane. Then gamma secretase makes the third cut, inside the membrane. It accepts a membrane protein only after most of the outer part is gone, so the second cut comes first.

scenes.visual: Three numbered cuts on the receptor: a seam present from the start (made earlier, no signal), the ADAM cut at the exposed spot (outer part goes into the sender with the ligand), then the gamma-secretase cut in the membrane that frees the inner part.
scenes.narration: In mammalian cells, the first cut comes while the receptor is made, and it carries no signal. After the pull, an ADAM protease makes the second cut, just outside the membrane. The outer part leaves with the ligand, and a stub stays in the membrane. Then γ-secretase makes the third cut, inside the membrane. It accepts a membrane protein only after most of the outer part is gone, so the second cut comes first.

scenes.tts: That cut frees the inner part of the receptor, which is called N I C D. It enters the nucleus, where a protein called C S L already sits on the target genes. In the standard account, C S L keeps those genes off with co-repressors. N I C D binds C S L, displaces the co-repressors, and recruits a co-activator called Mastermind. The genes turn on.
scenes.caption: That cut frees the inner part of the receptor, which is called NICD. It enters the nucleus, where a protein called CSL already sits on the target genes. In the standard account, CSL keeps those genes off with co-repressors. NICD binds CSL, displaces the co-repressors, and recruits a co-activator called Mastermind. The genes turn on.
scenes.visual: The view drops to the nucleus; the freed inner part travels in, CSL sits on the gene with co-repressors, the inner part joins CSL and pushes the co-repressors off, Mastermind arrives, and the gene switches on.
scenes.narration: That cut frees the inner part of the receptor, which is called NICD. It enters the nucleus, where a protein called CSL already sits on the target genes. In the standard account, CSL keeps those genes off with co-repressors. NICD binds CSL, displaces the co-repressors, and recruits a co-activator called Mastermind. The genes turn on.

scenes.tts: In a kinase cascade, each active enzyme modifies many substrates, so the signal grows at every step. Notch has no second messenger and no kinase relay. Between the membrane and the gene, nothing multiplies. One cut receptor gives one inner part. A cut cannot be undone, so each receptor signals once.
scenes.visual: Two lanes: a kinase cascade fans out from one enzyme to three to nine; Notch has crossed-out relay boxes and a single dot goes from one cut receptor to the gene, and the used receptor is spent.
scenes.narration: In a kinase cascade, each active enzyme modifies many substrates, so the signal grows at every step. Notch has no second messenger and no kinase relay. Between the membrane and the gene, nothing multiplies. One cut receptor gives one inner part. A cut cannot be undone, so each receptor signals once.

scenes.tts: What this design buys the cell is a count. The amount of inner part follows, one for one, the number of receptors a neighbour has pulled and cut. A cell hears Notch only from the cells it touches. Keep this rule: one receptor, pulled and cut, gives one inner part and one message.
scenes.visual: A neighbour pulls two receptors, then two more; each cut sends one inner part to the nucleus and two counters rise in step; the rule closes as one receptor, pulled and cut, gives one inner part and one message.
